status: Status: frozen (ADR-0119). Assigned values are immutable; a 'reserved...' construction may be filled once.
decoder_rules: exactly one top-level data item; trailing bytes -> trailing_bytes; truncated input -> truncated; reserved additional-info values 28..30 -> malformed; a break code (0xff) outside an indefinite item -> indefinite_length
integers and all length/count arguments use the shortest form (RFC 8949 §4.2.1) -> noncanonical_int / noncanonical_length
definite lengths only; additional info 31 anywhere -> indefinite_length
no tags (major 6) -> tag_forbidden (no tag is registered for W0)
simple values: only false (0xf4), true (0xf5) and null (0xf6); anything else, including undefined -> invalid_simple
text strings must be valid UTF-8 -> invalid_utf8 (no Unicode normalization is applied)
map keys are unsigned integers or text strings, and all keys of one map have the same major type -> key_type. This makes RFC 8949 §4.2.1 bytewise order and RFC 7049 §3.9 length-first order coincide.
map keys strictly increase in bytewise lexicographic order of their encodings; an equal key -> duplicate_key; a smaller key -> unsorted_keys
limits are checked before allocation: nesting depth, container item count, string byte length, and per-object max_bytes -> depth_limit / count_limit / size_limit
error_precedence: The first violation met in a depth-first, left-to-right walk wins. size_limit on the whole object is checked first. Decoder (encoding) checks complete before schema checks begin. A SignedEnvelope body is decoded and validated when its field is visited. Each negative vector contains exactly one violation, so precedence only matters for implementations that report more than one.

extensions.rule: Key 23 of a top-level object is a map of extension-id (tstr, 1..128 bytes) to ExtEntry {0: critical bool, 1: value any}. Registered IDs are mirrored in known_extensions and normatively defined by om-numeric-fields.json: owning object, exact criticality and registered payload schema are enforced. A registered extension with the wrong criticality is rejected. For a critical registration, a wrong owning object or an invalid payload also rejects the containing object; for a non-critical registration (critical=false on the wire and in the registry) a wrong owning object or an invalid payload makes the extension unusable and it is ignored semantically, so object validity never depends on the registry version a client ships (ADR-0155). An unknown extension with critical=true rejects the object (unknown_critical_extension). An unknown non-critical extension is normally ignored semantically and its bytes are preserved. ADR-0157 reserves extension IDs beginning with '!' as the registry-independent future-critical class: any unknown '!' ID rejects even when the wire critical bit is false; a registered '!' ID must be critical; and every new critical registration after the W0 freeze must use '!'. The only grandfathered critical IDs outside that class are om.acs.fork_ack and om.acs.legacy_policy, both already known to W0 decoders.
